_comment: Settings for suite_gen_inhibit.py (bench and emulated). One copy per machine, outside git; every <...> is a local path or name. The WiCAN SSID is never put here: the suite reads it from bench_holder. Keys the core reads: runs_root, bench_holder, bench_lock_log, canmain_check, hosts, esptool, wallclock_patterns, placement (shared/bench/README.md). placement (core 2026.11.12, Linux; AGENTS.md 'Parallel work on the shared machine', point 1): bench.slice for the lock and wallclock classes, build.slice for build and light, so every bench check starts in bench.slice and every emulated one in build.slice; with it the core refuses a bench run whose runner is not itself in bench.slice (start it with systemd-run --user --scope --slice=bench.slice). bench_lock_log puts the bench lock on that log; without it the Holder line of bench_holder is the lock, as before the cutover (shared/bench/SPEC.md (shared/main), section 7). Serial devices are named by their USB IDs, never a COM or tty name (DEVICES-SPEC S1, Linux only): esptool.device is the X2's, wican.usb_device the WiCAN's; the suite hands both to the tools as GI_X2_DEVICE and GI_WICAN_DEVICE. Serial numbers are bench identifiers: local settings only.

canmain_check.reason: <why this probe shows canmain down on this bench>

env.IDF_PATH: <the ESP-IDF v5.4.2 tree: C2scan's c_checks_run.py exports it>

argv: <the python of ESP-IDF v5.4.2's python env, whose esptool is 4.13.0>

chip.mac: <the X2's MAC, as esptool chip_id prints it>

_comment_wallclock_patterns: Regexes (re.search) over other processes' command lines that the core records in a wall-clock check's wallclock-others event as another wall-clock test running; recorded, never a refusal (AGENTS.md 'Parallel work on the shared machine', point 3). The charge-interposer's set (its accept_adapter.WALLCLOCK_PATTERNS: both projects' simulators and bench drivers, and the CAN replay tooling session's timing-sensitive scripts), and the Android emulator (gen-inhibit reviewer, 2026-11-23: bench run 4b15 shared bench.slice with both and its events named neither, the list being empty).
gi_commit: <the commit in the images' app descriptor, character for character: git's short form when they were built, which is 8 hex digits in this repo since 2026-11 (7 before); the suite compares it exactly, so a shorter or longer prefix of the same commit is refused as 'code is not identifiable'. The bench run looks for an emulated run on the same string, so give both runs the same one>
gi_can1_termination: <where the CAN1 terminators are, as read on the bench by a person; NONODE's --termination>
gi_wican_power: <how the WiCAN is powered, as read on the bench by a person (12 V on OBD pin 16; USB plugged or not); B5_B8's records carry it>
interposer_code: <a read-only detached checkout of charge-interposer/main at interposer_code_commit>/charge-interposer
interposer_code_commit: <that commit, as the checkout's HEAD starts; the bench suite refuses a checkout not clean at it>

ota._comment: The core flasher's block (vtrux_bench.run.ota, core 2026.11.16.5; FLASH-SPEC O2): the WiCAN's OTA and every join of its hotspot use it, the tools getting it as GI_OTA_SETTINGS. wifi adb is the phone over adb (FLASH-SPEC O4): iface its Wi-Fi interface, profile its saved network's id for the hotspot, adb_serial its adb serial (a bench identifier: local settings only). wifi system is the host's own adapter (iface its device, profile its saved profile). ssid_env names the variable the suite fills with bench-holder.md's SSID; the SSID itself is never here.
ota.profile: <the phone's saved network id for the hotspot>
ota.capture_iface: <the host's RNDIS link to the phone, as dumpcap -D names it>

x2_pin_dir: <folder holding <pin>/<image>/<file> for x2_pin.json, e.g. <reverse-it>/projects/vtrux/notes/artifacts/gen-inhibit/x2_pin; filled by x2_pin.py install. Only where the files are: their bytes and the X2's identities are the committed pin's, and the old x2_images setting is refused>
_comment_serial_port: No serial_port: the interposer's bench_identify reads settings.serial_port, and the suite hands it a copy of these settings with serial_port set to the X2's by-id path, resolved from esptool.device (recorded in the identify step's serial_device_bench_identify.txt).
